text:
sam: Heads up — hitting a mypy error when using the async Python SDK in an async with context. Stubs don't show __aenter__/__aexit__ on AsyncClient so the typechecker complains.

maria: ugh. can you paste a tiny repro?

sam: yep. minimal:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=...) as c:  # mypy: "AsyncClient" has no attribute "__aenter__"
        await c.generate("hi")
```

maria: that helps. runtime works fine right? it's only a typing issue?

sam: runtime is fine, it's strictly the .pyi/.stubs we ship. mypy 1.6 rejects it. pyright also flags it. :facepalm:

raj: think the generator emits `class AsyncClient:` without async context manager dunders. We probably only added close()/__exit__ on sync client.

lee: quick workaround: annotate with typing.cast(Any, AsyncClient(...)) or avoid async with (ugh). better to add `async def __aenter__(self) -> "AsyncClient": ...` & `async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None: ...` in the stub.

maria: adding to generator seems right. Also need to ensure return type for __aenter__ is Self/AsyncClient so async with binds name correctly.

raj: agree. another twist: our auth middleware exposes refresh_token as a coroutine on the client, but stubs mark it as Callable[..., None] — so callers `await client.auth.refresh_token()` are flagged. I can include that fix in the same generator patch.

sam: nice — two problems in one. Can we also make sure the streaming API stub types an AsyncIterator[bytes] or a concrete chunk TypedDict instead of AsyncIterator[Any]? It's causing a bunch of downstream mypy noise in sample apps.

lee: yes, streaming chunk type should be a concrete TypedDict we generate, not Any. We'll update the shape generator to emit TypedDict definitions and reference them in iterator signatures.

maria: plan: (1) generator: add proper async context manager dunders on AsyncClient, (2) fix auth.refresh_token typing to be `async def refresh_token(...) -> str`, (3) emit TypedDicts for streaming chunks and use `AsyncIterator[StreamChunk]`, (4) run mypy+pyright on sampleapps in CI to catch regressions.

raj: +1. I'll open a PR to the autogen repo and include a unit that compiles the generated stubs with mypy and pyright. cc @devex-bot to add the CI job.

devex-bot: created issue #412: "async client stubs: context-manager + auth + stream typing" and assigned to raj. CI job mypy-sampleapp added to pipeline.

sam: thanks! one more micro-request — can the stubs use typing.Self on fluent methods (where methods return self) to help pyright inference?

lee: yep. We'll emit `from typing import Self` for py3.11+ targets and fall back to the class name string for older compatibility.

maria: if anyone wants a pairing session on the generator changes lmk — I'd like to make sure the TypedDict/field names match the SDK docs to avoid churn.

sam: I can test against our customer sampleapp that surfaced this. appreciate the quick turnaround 🙏 :heart:
